en: For the rest and the pleasure of the soldier,
There is, over there, two steps from the forest,
A house with walls all covered in ivy;
“Aux Tourlourous” is the name of the tavern.
The serving girl is young and nice,
Light as a butterfly.
Like her wine, her eye sparkles;
We call her the Madelon.
We dream of it at night, we think of it by day;
It is only Madelon, but for us it is love.
Refrain:
When Madelon comes to pour us something to drink,
Under the arbour we brush against her petticoat,
And each of us tells her a story,
A story in his own way.
The Madelon is not strict with us
When we take her by the waist or the chin;
She laughs, that is all the harm she knows how to do.
Madelon, Madelon, Madelon!
We all have back home a girl from our parts
Who is waiting for us and whom we will marry,
But she is far away, much too far for us to tell her
What we will do when our class goes home.
Counting the days, we sigh,
And when the time seems long to us,
All that we cannot tell her
We go and tell Madelon.
We kiss her in the corners. She says, “Will you stop…”
We imagine she is the other one; that pleases us a lot.
A corporal in a fancy kepi
Went to find Madelon one fine morning
And, mad with love, told her she was pretty
And that he had come to ask for her hand.
The Madelon, no fool after all,
Answered him with a smile:
And why would I take one man alone
When I love a whole regiment?
Your friends will come. You will not have my hand;
I need it far too much to pour them wine.
notes: line 1.4: 'Tourlourou' is old soldiers' slang for an infantryman; the tavern's name means 'At the Foot Soldiers''. Kept as a name.
line 1.8: 'la Madelon' is a familiar form of Madeleine; the article before a woman's name is colloquial.
line 2.1: 'Refrain :' is a label and is kept.
line 3.1: 'une payse' is colloquial for a girl from one's own village or district, a sweetheart back home.
line 3.4: 'quand la classe rentrera' = when the class goes home: 'la classe' is the year's intake of conscripts, sent home together at the end of their service.
line 3.9: 'veux-tu finir…' = will you stop (that)…, a mild protest.
line 3.10: 'On s'figure' is spoken French for 'on se figure', we imagine; 'l'autre' is the sweetheart at home.
line 4.1: 'képi de fantaisie' = a kepi not of the regulation pattern, a smart one bought privately.
line 4.10: 'main' plays on the hand asked in marriage (4.4) and the hand that pours the wine.
